citations.quote: RINVOQ is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor indicated for the treatment of adults with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis who have had an inadequate response or intolerance to methotrexate. (1)

target_moa.text: Upadacitinib is an oral, selective Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor (selective JAK-1 inhibitor) that modulates the signaling pathway at the point of JAKs, preventing phosphorylation and activation of STATs and thereby modulating immune cell function.

citations.quote: Upadacitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor. JAKs are intracellular enzymes which transmit signals arising from cytokine or growth factor-receptor interactions on the cellular membrane to
Upadacitinib modulates the signaling pathway at the point of JAKs, preventing the phosphorylation and activation of STATs.
The drug substance, upadacitinib, is proposed by the Applicant to be a novel, oral, selective, reversible JAK-1 inhibitor.
AbbVie submitted new drug application (NDA) 211675 on December 18, 2018, for the new molecular entity (NME) upadacitinib, an oral small molecule inhibitor of the Janus associated kinases (JAK)

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (>=1%) were upper respiratory tract infection (13.5% RINVOQ 15 mg vs 9.5% placebo), nausea (3.5% vs 2.2%), cough (2.2% vs 1.0%), and pyrexia (1.2% vs 0%). Serious risks include serious infections, malignancy, thrombosis, gastrointestinal perforations, and laboratory abnormalities.

detail.text: Boxed warning: SERIOUS INFECTIONS, MALIGNANCY, AND THROMBOSIS. Serious infections leading to hospitalization or death (including tuberculosis, bacterial, invasive fungal, viral and other opportunistic infections); lymphoma and other malignancies; and thrombosis (deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and arterial thrombosis) have occurred.

citations.quote: ## WARNING: SERIOUS INFECTIONS, MALIGNANCY, AND THROMBOSIS

Serious infections leading to hospitalization or death, including tuberculosis and bacterial, invasive fungal, viral, and other opportunistic infections, have occurred in patients receiving RINVOQ. (5.1)
Thrombosis, including deep venous thrombosis, pulmonary embolism, and arterial thrombosis have occurred in patients treated with Janus kinase inhibitors used to treat inflammatory conditions.

detail.text: A Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) was determined not necessary because the risks can be adequately described in product labeling.

summary.text: RINVOQ (upadacitinib), a new molecular entity oral small-molecule JAK inhibitor, was submitted by AbbVie on December 18, 2018 and reviewed under Priority Review supported by a Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher, with a PDUFA goal date of August 18, 2019. It was approved (first cycle, no advisory committee) for moderately to severely active RA in MTX inadequate responders; no REMS was required and pediatric studies were required under PREA.

citations.quote: AbbVie submitted new drug application (NDA) 211675 on December 18, 2018, for the new molecular entity (NME) upadacitinib, an oral small molecule inhibitor of the Janus associated kinases (JAK)
The Applicant requested a Priority Review and used Rare Pediatric Disease Priority Review Voucher No. PRV BLA 125516 to support their request.

Given that the safety profile of upadacitinib is generally consistent with other immunosuppressants and JAK inhibitors approved for RA patients, the risks can be adequately described in product labeling and a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) is not necessary.
An advisory committee meeting was not held for this application. No issues were identified warranting advisory committee input.
